sources.outlet: Deportation Data Project (UC Berkeley / UCLA law)
sources.quote: First, detainer requests from ICE to local jails and state prisons rose sharply in 2026. ICE increased the number of such requests by increasingly targeting noncitizens without criminal convictions.
sources.searcher_note: Post-cutoff. Same direction (detainers shifting toward no-conviction people), counts by month in a chart; no share percentage stated in text.

sources.quote: Out of 17,972 detainers issued between January 20 and February 17, just 28 percent had any prior conviction.
sources.searcher_note: Early-2025 window only; same page adds Feb 18-Mar 18 2025 at 25.6 percent. Our lead has Oct-Mar FY25 at 33%, a different window.

sources.quote: ICE records indicated that 97 percent of all detainers issued during the Biden years were for immigrants who had been charged or convicted of a crime.
sources.searcher_note: Different definition: charged OR convicted, not convicted only; Biden-years window. Not a conviction-only share.

notes: No source found stating the conviction-only share of detainers for FY23 (43%) or FY26 (16%), or the FY23-to-FY26 drop. Most 2026 coverage (TRAC quick facts, Cato, Poynter, FactCheck, Stateline) is about the detention population or arrests, not detainers; those were not recorded. Deportation Data Project (post-cutoff) states the direction for detainers in words. TRAC gives early-2025 detainer conviction shares (28%, 25.6%) for windows that do not line up with the lead's Oct-Mar comparison. DHS press releases describe individual detainers only; no aggregate share that disagrees.
